author: Japanese Research Division, Military History Section, Headquarters, Army Forces Far East
title: Japanese Monograph No. 97: Pearl Harbor Operations — General Outline of Orders and Plans
publisher: Military History Section, Headquarters, Army Forces Far East, Tokyo
notes: The one monograph of the series this project has so far leaned on hard enough to earn its own entry, as source:japanese-monographs said one would. It is the Hawaii operation reduced to its orders: the task organisation of the striking force ship by ship, the speed it was to sail at, the named points it was to pass through, the hours the two waves were to be launched, and what was to happen after them. Everything this pack says about what the operation was *supposed* to do comes from here. Read it under the series' own warning, which is quoted in full in source:japanese-monographs: the originals were destroyed before the surrender and much of this was reconstructed from memory by the officers who had held the appointments, so it is evidence of what a Japanese commander said the plan was, in the manner of a memoir, and not the text of an order. Two internal inconsistencies were noticed and are not resolved here: the standby point is given as 42°N 165°W on p. 7 and as 42°N 170°W on p. 21, and the aircraft totals differ from those Fuchida gave the US Strategic Bombing Survey in 1945 (source:ussbs-interrogations). No year is recorded because the transcription carries none; the series ran from 1946 to 1960. Pages are as marked in the HyperWar transcription at ibiblio.org, which is a transcription and not a page scan — see the pack README on how far this project can promise a page number read through it.
